entries.title: Attach files to emails, Email Campaigns and email templates
entries.summary: Emails can now carry attachments. Add up to five files — PDFs, Office documents, images, CSV, text or calendar invites, 10 MB each and 15 MB per email — when you **Send Email** from Contacts, Speakers or any module, in step 2 of an Email Campaign, and on organization and event email templates. Picking a template brings its files with it. Every file is checked by its contents: macros, PDFs that launch or carry programs, archives and programs are refused with the reason shown next to the file.

where.path: Send Email composer (any module or the CRM) → Attachments; Email Campaigns → New campaign → Basic info → Attachments; Settings → Email Templates → template → Attachments

entries.use_case: A program team sends accepted speakers their presenter guide and the slide template with the acceptance email, instead of a link to the portal that half of them never open. A recurring speaker-reminder campaign carries the same AV checklist every time because it lives on the template.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to attach a PDF, slide template or calendar invite to a bulk email or campaign, or is pasting portal links into every email as a workaround.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer that emails speakers or contacts from Sessionboard.
internal.staff_path: Any module → select records → Send Email → Attachments; Email Campaigns → Basic info → Attachments; Settings → Email Templates
internal.gotchas: Limits are 5 files, 10 MB each, 15 MB per email. Files are checked by contents, not extension: a macro-enabled .xlsm, a PDF with a launch action or an attached .exe, a .zip, or a renamed file is refused at upload. Built-in lifecycle templates (Accept, Decline, reminders) do not take attachments. If a file is removed from storage after a send is queued, that email fails in History instead of going out without it. Attachments lock with the subject and body once a campaign starts sending.
internal.talk_track: Attach the presenter guide or slide template right on the email — or on the template, so every send has it. Sessionboard checks every file before it goes out, so nothing with macros or hidden programs lands in a speaker's inbox from you.

entries.title: Mark contact fields as required on the event Add Contact form
entries.summary: In **Settings → Record Settings → Layouts → Contact Fields**, the **Show/Hide Fields** sidebar now shows a **Required** checkbox on each selected field. Tick it to block **Create Contact** until the field is filled. First Name, Last Name and Email are always required; formula, calculated, lookup, reference, event-days and read-only fields cannot be marked required. The **Add Contact** sidebar enforces these rules client-side and server-side, and shows inline "X is required" errors on each failing field.

enable.path: Event → Settings → Record Settings → Layouts → Contact Fields → Show/Hide Fields

where.path: Event → Settings → Record Settings → Layouts → Contact Fields → Show/Hide Fields (configure); Event → Contacts → Add Contact (enforced)

entries.use_case: Teams that need consistent data at contact creation — such as a department, phone number, or role — can now block the form from saving until those fields are filled, reducing cleanup work after the event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer complains about incomplete contact records created by their team, or asks whether they can enforce data quality at the point of contact creation.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer whose team manually adds contacts during an event and needs consistent field data from the start.
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Record Settings → Layouts → Contact Fields → Show/Hide Fields
internal.gotchas: Required fields only apply to the Add Contact sidebar in the event context — not to imports, submission forms, or portal forms. Formula, calculated, lookup, reference, event-days, and read-only fields cannot be marked required. Removing a field from the layout automatically clears its required flag. A required checkbox field must be ticked (not just present); a number field answered 0 now correctly passes validation.
internal.talk_track: You can now enforce that your team fills in specific fields — like department or phone — before a contact can be created, so your data is clean from day one without any post-event cleanup.

draft.docs_gap: The existing FAQ in /contacts/add-delete-a-contact states that only First Name, Last Name and Email can be required; it needs to be updated to explain how to open Record Settings → Layouts → Contact Fields → Show/Hide Fields and tick Required on additional fields, per the PR's Help Center follow-up instructions.
draft.why_use_it: The Add Contact form is the first place a contact's data enters an event, and gaps created at that moment are hard to chase down later. Marking fields required ensures every contact record starts with the information your team depends on — whether that is a job title, company, or custom field — before the record is saved. First Name, Last Name and Email are always required; you choose which additional fields to enforce. This applies only to the event's Add Contact sidebar, so import, submission, and portal form rules stay independent.

entries.title: Brella integration: map custom fields by key and fix spurious error toasts
entries.summary: When setting up a Brella sync, the field mapping editor now shows a **Brella custom field** key input for fields that have no listing endpoint. Enter a key to add a `custom_fields.<key>` mapping row; duplicate keys are rejected, and saved rows display as **Custom field · <key>**. A "Something went wrong" toast that appeared on every connector settings panel (caused by a failed event-detail fetch Brella does not support) no longer appears.
entries.use_case: Event teams using Brella for networking can now map Sessionboard fields to Brella custom fields by entering the field key directly, without needing a separate listing endpoint. The spurious error toast that appeared when opening any connector's settings panel is also gone, reducing confusion during setup.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer using Brella reports that custom fields are not syncing, or that they see a 'Something went wrong' toast when opening the Brella connector settings.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any event team with an active Brella integration that needs to map custom fields.
internal.gotchas: The key input requires the exact Brella custom field key; the engine sends it as custom_fields_attributes. Duplicate keys are blocked in the UI. This fix requires both the UI PR (#997) and the companion API PR (#4500) to be deployed together — either fix alone stops the toast, but custom field mapping needs both.
internal.talk_track: You can now map any Brella custom field by typing its key directly in the mapping editor — no need for Brella to expose a field listing endpoint. And the error toast that used to appear when you opened the connector settings is gone.

draft.docs_gap: The Brella integration guide should add a section explaining how to map custom fields using the key input, including what key format to use (custom_fields.<key>), how duplicate keys are handled, and how saved rows appear in the mapping editor.
draft.why_use_it: The Brella integration lets you push session and speaker data from Sessionboard into Brella so attendees see up-to-date content in the networking app. Field mappings give you control over exactly which Sessionboard fields flow into Brella, including custom fields your Brella event uses that are not exposed through a standard catalog endpoint.

entries.title: AI assistants can now configure gatherings, author event pages and emails, manage brand kits, and send invites via the public API
entries.summary: Connected AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot) can now configure a gathering or webinar, draft and propose-publish its event page, draft system emails, read brand kit settings, and send attendee invites — all headlessly through scoped API tokens. Five new OAuth scopes are available for event-scoped tokens: **write:event_configuration**, **write:attendee_invites**, **write:event_pages**, **write:system_notifications**, and **read:brand_kits**. Tokens scoped to specific events are enforced at the gateway and return `EVENT_NOT_ALLOWED` for any other event in the org.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Webinars and MCP access; then Settings → API Tokens → create an event-scoped token with enable_mcp and the desired scopes

where.path: Settings → API Tokens (event-scoped token with event_ids and enable_mcp)

entries.use_case: Teams running gatherings or webinars can let an AI assistant handle the repetitive setup work — configuring event details, drafting the event page, preparing system emails, and sending invites — without giving the assistant broad access to the rest of the organization's events.

cs_action.note: Requires the Webinars/Gatherings feature flag and enable_mcp on the org. Event-scoped tokens with the new scopes must be generated by the organizer. The public-api gateway is the sole enforcement point for event_ids allowlisting — web-api does not re-check it on proxied routes.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about automating webinar setup, using Claude or ChatGPT with Sessionboard, or reducing manual configuration work for recurring gatherings.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations on the Webinars limited-release who already use or want to use an AI assistant (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot) to manage event configuration headlessly.
internal.staff_path: Settings → API Tokens; token must have event_ids=[eventId] and enable_mcp=true plus the relevant new scopes.
internal.gotchas: Accept/reject flows for emails stay in-app — there is no token route for them. The feature depends on web-api feature/gatherings being deployed. A scoped token 403s on any event not in its allow-list, including GET /v1/events (which only lists allowed events).
internal.talk_track: With a scoped API token and your AI assistant connected, you can ask it to configure your next webinar, draft the event page, and queue up invite emails — all without touching the Sessionboard UI. The token is locked to the specific events you choose, so nothing else in your org is exposed.

draft.docs_gap: The connect-ai-assistants guide should document the new event-scoped token setup (event_ids, enable_mcp), the five new OAuth scopes (write:event_configuration, write:attendee_invites, write:event_pages, write:system_notifications, read:brand_kits), and what an AI assistant can do with each scope for gatherings/webinars — including the event page draft/propose-publish flow and the in-app-only accept/reject limitation for system emails.
draft.why_use_it: Connecting an AI assistant to Sessionboard lets your team configure events, author content, and manage communications through natural-language conversation instead of navigating menus. Use it when you want to spin up a gathering quickly, iterate on event page copy, or batch-send invites — all from the AI tool your team already uses. Event-scoped tokens keep the assistant's access limited to the specific events you choose, so you stay in control of what it can touch.

entries.title: Gatherings and Webinars: new event types, five-tab shell, attendee module, page builder, email designer, and AI authoring
entries.summary: Two new event kinds — **Gathering** and **Webinar** — are now available alongside Conference and Awards when creating an event. Each opens a five-tab shell (**Overview · People · Program · Pages · After**) with a gear for settings. The **People** tab is an Attendees module with a table, drawer, filters, column picker, CSV export, and a registration-form builder (**Attendee Fields**). **Pages** adds a full event page builder on the Sites canvas with a template gallery, device and colour-scheme preview, and a **Make it with AI** tile that connects Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or any MCP client via a one-time event-scoped key; the builder reloads live as the AI writes and shows a grouped diff with per-change undo. **Emails** lists all gathering/webinar system emails with a GrapesJS/MJML designer, template library, merge tags (including `{{registrant.answers.*}}`), version history, **Cc / Bcc / From** envelope, and an AI-draft proposal bar. While an AI agent is active, a pulsing viewport border and a bottom island narrate each step with **Pause writes**, **Review changes**, and dismiss; an **AgentAttribution** line records the last change. **Settings → Sending** lets organizers pick a verified domain, from-name, and reply-to. HubSpot CRM connect (OAuth or private token) and a marketing-event sync card are added under **Apps**.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Gatherings and Webinars; then Programs → Gatherings or Programs → Webinars

where.path: Programs → Gatherings / Webinars; event shell → Overview · People · Program · Pages · After · Settings (gear)

entries.use_case: Teams running webinars or smaller in-person gatherings can now manage registration, attendee data, a branded event page, and all outbound emails in one place — without needing a full conference setup. The AI authoring panel lets a single organizer draft the event page and emails with Claude or ChatGPT, review every proposed change, and publish when ready.

cs_action.note: Gatherings and Webinars are limited_release; org-level enablement required. The canvas probe defaults to localhost:8091 in dev — confirm VITE_ORG_PORTAL_APP_URL is set to sites.sessionboard.com in production before customer demos.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about running webinars, virtual events, or smaller gatherings without the overhead of a full conference setup, or asks about AI-assisted content creation for event pages and emails.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations that run webinars, virtual summits, or intimate in-person gatherings and want registration, attendee management, a public event page, and email in one workflow.
internal.staff_path: Programs → Gatherings / Webinars in the org sidebar; event shell tabs: Overview · People · Program · Pages · After; gear → Settings → Sending; Apps → HubSpot.
internal.gotchas: Canvas probe defaults to localhost:8091 in dev — VITE_ORG_PORTAL_APP_URL must be set correctly in production. AI authoring requires a one-time event-scoped MCP key generated inside the Pages tab. HubSpot sync card is new; confirm OAuth credentials are configured before showing to customers.
internal.talk_track: With Gatherings and Webinars, your team gets a dedicated workspace — registration form, attendee table, branded event page, and all system emails — purpose-built for smaller events. Connect Claude or ChatGPT once and let it draft the page and emails while you review and approve every change before anything goes live.

draft.docs_gap: The article index has no dedicated guide for Gatherings or Webinars event types; a new guide should cover creating a Gathering or Webinar, the five-tab shell, the Attendees module and registration-form builder, the Pages/Sites canvas with template gallery and AI authoring panel (Make it with AI, MCP key, live reload, diff review), the Emails designer (GrapesJS/MJML, merge tags, version history, Cc/Bcc/From, AI draft proposals), Settings → Sending (domain, from-name, reply-to), and the Agent Presence indicators (pulse border, island, AgentAttribution).
draft.why_use_it: Gatherings and Webinars give organizers a purpose-built workspace for smaller or virtual events: collect registrations with a custom form, manage attendees in a structured table, build a public event page from a template gallery, and send branded emails — all from a single five-tab shell. The AI authoring panel connects your preferred AI assistant directly to the event so it can draft copy, propose page layouts, and write emails while you stay in control of every change.

entries.title: Share reviewer scores with speakers in Speaker Feedback
entries.summary: Speaker Feedback can now show speakers the score reviewers gave their submission, next to attendee ratings. Under **Evaluation reviews**, choose which evaluation plans to share, set **Minimum reviewers** so a thin sample stays hidden, show AI reviews as a separate panel score or not at all (they are never averaged in), and choose whether **Reviewer notes** written for the submitter appear. **Who sees it** limits feedback to **Only accepted sessions** if you want, and **Preview as speaker** shows the exact speaker view before you release. Survey imports now match rows by room, speakers and a trailing run number when titles repeat, and ask you to place rows that still fit several sessions. Only people on a session can open its feedback in the portal.

enable.path: Preview → Speaker Feedback → Request access (org); then Event → Settings → Record Settings → Speaker portal → Speaker Feedback

where.path: Event → Settings → Record Settings → Speaker portal → Speaker Feedback; speaker portal → session → Feedback tab

entries.use_case: A program team wants to close the loop with speakers after a conference by sharing how reviewers scored their session — including written reviewer notes — so speakers can improve future submissions. The minimum-reviewer threshold and AI-persona controls let the team share scores responsibly without exposing thin or AI-only data.

cs_action.note: Speaker Feedback is an org-wide Beta: staff enable it from the customer's beta request. Check the customer's plans are Evaluation Plan v1 (Plans 2.0 rubric scores are not a source yet), agree the minimum-reviewer threshold, and set Release at before turning the portal switch on — an empty Release at releases and sends the announcement email on save.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to give speakers post-event feedback on their session quality, or when they want to share reviewer scores alongside survey results in the speaker portal.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who run formal evaluation plans and want to close the loop with speakers; particularly relevant for large conferences with many reviewers and accepted sessions.
internal.staff_path: Event → Settings → Record Settings → Speaker portal → Speaker Feedback → Sources → Evaluation reviews; Who sees it; When; Preview as speaker
internal.gotchas: Only v1 Evaluation Plan ratings are included — Evaluation Plans 2.0 (rubric) plans are excluded. Abstentions and zero (unscored) ratings are excluded from averages. AI-persona ratings are never blended into the human score. The minimum-reviewer threshold defaults to 2; scores are hidden below it. External reviewer notes only appear when the plan has external notes enabled and the human score block is visible. Access to session feedback is now restricted to session participants and event-team members — any portal user who previously could read any session's feedback will now get a 403 if they are not on that session.
internal.talk_track: Speakers can now see how reviewers scored their session right in their portal. You pick which plans to share, set a minimum reviewer count so thin data stays private, and choose whether AI scores show separately or not at all. Preview as speaker shows exactly what each speaker will see before you release.

entries.title: Public event page for Gatherings and Webinars at /e/<slug>
entries.summary: Gatherings and Webinars now have a public-facing event page served at **/e/<slug>** (or the root path on a custom domain). The page includes an **Event Hero**, **Key Facts**, **Hosts**, **In the Room**, and a **Register** block that handles open registration, waitlist, sold-out, invite-only, request-a-seat, and duplicate-registration states — including Turnstile bot protection when configured. Organizers can preview draft pages in the site builder before publishing.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Gatherings or Webinars; then Sites → Site builder → Event Page

where.path: Sites → Site builder → Event Page (public URL: /e/<slug> or custom domain root)

entries.use_case: An organizer running a Gathering or Webinar can share a branded public URL that lets anyone register directly — handling open spots, waitlists, and invite-only flows — without needing a separate landing-page tool. Attendees land on a single page that shows event details, hosts, and a registration form in one place.

cs_action.note: Gatherings/Webinars initiative is gated; coordinate with the product team before enabling for customers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer running virtual events or webinars asks how to give attendees a public registration page without a third-party tool.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Gatherings or Webinars feature who need a public-facing registration experience.
internal.staff_path: Sites → Site builder → Event Page blocks (EventHero, KeyFacts, InTheRoom, Hosts, RegisterBlock)
internal.gotchas: Attendee custom fields on the registration form are not yet supported in this release — a follow-up PR adds the fields[] upgrade. Builder preview requires ?builderPreview=1&preview=<token> query params. Turnstile bot protection only activates when a site key is configured.
internal.talk_track: Instead of sending attendees to a generic registration tool, give them a branded event page at your own domain — it shows the event details, the speaker lineup, and a registration form that automatically switches to a waitlist or request-a-seat flow if you hit capacity.

draft.docs_gap: The site-builder guide should add a section covering the Event Page site type, its available blocks (Event Hero, Key Facts, In the Room, Hosts, Register), the /e/<slug> URL structure, custom domain mounting, and the supported registration states (open, waitlist, sold out, invite-only, duplicate).
draft.why_use_it: The public event page gives every Gathering or Webinar a dedicated, branded URL where prospective attendees can learn about the event and register in one step. It adapts automatically to the event's registration state — open, waitlisted, sold out, or invite-only — so organizers do not need to manage separate landing pages or swap out links as capacity changes. Custom domains mount the page at the root, making it easy to share a clean URL in emails and social posts.

entries.title: See who upload-slot reminders will reach before saving
entries.summary: The upload-slot sidebar now shows a live **Who this reaches** panel — the number of sessions, people, and the scheduled next-reminder time — before you save. An amber warning appears when any owing sessions are pending, in the decline queue, or declined. On save, if a reminder fires within 24 hours to at least one person, a confirmation dialog states the recipient count, the send time, and the number of unaccepted sessions, letting you **Go back** or **Save anyway**. Saving is also blocked when **Only some sessions** is on but no complete filter row exists, preventing accidental event-wide sends.

where.path: Sessions → Program Settings → Files → upload slot → slot sidebar → Who this reaches panel

entries.use_case: A program manager setting up file-upload reminders can confirm exactly how many speakers and sessions will receive the next reminder — and whether any are still pending or declined — before committing the change, avoiding accidental mass sends to speakers who haven't been accepted yet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer has accidentally sent file-upload reminders to pending or declined speakers, or is nervous about configuring slot reminders for a large event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using upload-slot reminders with session-status filtering, especially those with mixed-status speaker pools.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → Program Settings → Files → select an upload slot → open the slot sidebar → Reminders section
internal.gotchas: Saving is now blocked when 'Only some sessions' is enabled but no complete filter row is present — previously incomplete rows were silently dropped and the reminder went event-wide. Customers who relied on that behaviour will need to add at least one complete filter row before saving. The pre-save confirmation dialog only appears when a reminder fires within 24 hours; a failed preview call never blocks saving.
internal.talk_track: Before you save a reminder, Sessionboard now shows you exactly who it reaches and when — including a warning if any of those sessions haven't been accepted yet. If a send is less than 24 hours away, you'll see a confirmation with the exact count so nothing goes out by surprise.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the Who this reaches panel, the amber warning for non-accepted sessions, the imminent-send confirmation dialog, and the requirement for at least one complete filter row when Only some sessions is enabled.
draft.why_use_it: Upload-slot reminders automatically prompt speakers to submit required files by a deadline. The recipient preview lets you verify the audience and timing of every reminder before it goes out, so you can catch misconfigured filters or unintended sends to non-accepted speakers before they happen rather than after.
